policy: Every rewrite the compiler applies to emitted CSS is an entry here; the stage applies nothing else. The rewrite takes no target, host, file or ordering input, so CSS bytes never depend on targets.

kind prefix-alias: a declaration of `property` whose value is in `values` is preceded, in the same declaration block, by `variant` with the identical value. The standard form stays last, so an engine that parses both uses it.

An entry requires: the variant is, on every announced engine at the O13 floor, an alias of the base (CE-00.1 vendor-legacy-variant, never divergent-legacy-variant), the only form, or dropped at parse time; every admitted value of the base is in `values`; and a proof with a rationale, fixture ids and the evidence classes executed and deferred.
A renamed value (an alternative name such as -webkit-fill-available) is never a prefix alias.

proof.rationale: BCD 8.1.6 records unprefixed user-select on Chromium 54+, Firefox 69+ and Firefox Android 79+, and only in preview on Safari; -webkit-user-select ships on every announced engine at the O13 floor (Chrome 1, Chrome Android 18, Edge 12, WebView 4.4, Firefox and Firefox Android 49, Safari and iOS Safari 3). CE-00.1 classifies -webkit-user-select as vendor-legacy-variant of user-select (docs/research/core-evolution-registry.v1.json). Where both parse they are one property, so the pair in one block keeps the rule's selector, specificity, layer and order position: the cascade picks the same rule for both. Every value of the shared subset is paired, so a descendant's own value overrides an ancestor's value in both forms even if an engine inherits the prefixed form.

deferred.check: Whether WebKit treats -webkit-user-select as inherited, and that a descendant's paired value overrides an ancestor's none (computed value and selection behavior).
